days.title: Low Tide Formations and Arches
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: playa de Aguas Santas
stops.detail: The Beach of the Cathedrals (in Galician, praia das Catedrais) is the tourist name of the Beach of Holy Waters (in Galician, praia de Augas Santas), located in the Galician municipality of Ribadeo (Devesa parish), on the coast of the province of Lugo, Spain, on the Cantabrian Sea.

stops.name: arcos
stops.detail: Characteristic of the beach are the arches and sea caves, only visible at the foot of the beach during low tide.

stops.name: grutas
stops.detail: During low tide, one can access a long sandy area bordered by a rocky wall of slate and schist eroded into whimsical shapes: arches over thirty meters high resembling cathedral flying buttresses, grottoes tens of meters long, sand corridors between rock blocks, and other curiosities.

stops.name: acantilados
stops.detail: It is known by this name due to the appearance of its cliffs.

stops.name: playa de Esteiro
stops.detail: It is interesting to see the beach at high tide by walking along the top of the cliffs in a west-east direction towards Esteiro beach and to see it at low tide on the beach sand.

stops.name: miradores
stops.detail: Adjacent to the beach parking lot, two viewpoints can be found from where you can contemplate in their entirety the magnificent views of the Mariña lucense.
